mainTopic: Examining a בכור's blemish on יום טוב, and whether there is מוקצה for half of שבת
overview: The amud opens with the end of a ברייתא about a בכור (firstborn animal) whose blemish is examined on יום טוב. רבה בר רב הונא teaches that a בכור born with its blemish may be examined even לכתחילה. רב נחמן objects from his father's teaching that it works only בדיעבד. אביי defends רבה בר רב הונא by reading the ברייתא as three levels of permission. The גמרא then brings רב אושעיא's ברייתא, which reads differently, and dismisses אביי's ברייתא as the mixed-up version of אדא בר אוכמי. רב נחמן בר יצחק proves from the wording of the משנה that the examination is valid only בדיעבד. Next, הלל asks רבא whether something can be מוקצה for half of שבת: fit, then unfit, then fit again. Two versions of רבא's answer are given. Proofs from the blemished בכור and from fruit drying on the roof are both pushed aside. רבי זירא begins a new proof from beans and lentils cooked on יום טוב, and it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the ברייתא: a blemish that appeared on יום טוב versus one the animal was born with
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון rules that a בכור whose blemish appeared on יום טוב is not מוכן. All agree that a בכור born with its blemish is מוכן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the blemish appeared on the Festival itself, רבי שמעון says this animal is not counted as 'prepared' for the Festival. Everyone agrees that if the animal was born with its blemish, it is counted as 'prepared.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא that started earlier. It gives רבי שמעון's ruling about a blemish that appeared on יום טוב, and a case everyone agrees on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food used on יום טוב must have been 'ready' before the holiday began. When the blemish appears on יום טוב itself, the animal was not fit to eat when the holiday started, so רבי שמעון says it is not מוכן. When the animal was born already blemished, it was fit from birth, so both sides agree it is מוכן.

keyTerms.meaning: Among the things 'prepared' (ready for use) before יום טוב began
And they agree (both sides of the argument)
It was born with its blemish already on it
A blemish, which allows a בכור to be slaughtered and eaten

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this is the start of a new teaching. These words finish a ברייתא that began just before this section.

phrases.english: on the Festival, Rabbi Shimon says:
phrases.notes: This finishes a line that began earlier: if the animal developed a blemish on the Festival itself.

phrases.english: This is not among the prepared.

phrases.aramaic: וְשָׁוִין שֶׁאִם נוֹלַד הוּא וּמוּמוֹ עִמּוֹ
phrases.english: And they agree that if it was born with its blemish
that this is among the prepared.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אֵין זֶה מִן הַמּוּכָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A blemish that appeared on יום טוב makes the animal not מוכן according to רבי שמעון. An animal born with its blemish is מוכן according to everyone.

steps.title: רבה בר רב הונא: an animal born blemished may be examined on יום טוב from the start
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא teaches publicly that a בכור born with its blemish may be examined on יום טוב even לכתחילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא taught: if the animal was born with its blemish, we may examine it on the Festival, even from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר רב הונא gives a practical ruling based on the last line of the ברייתא. He permits examining the animal on יום טוב even לכתחילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only said the animal is מוכן. רבה בר רב הונא adds that this means full permission. The examination may be done on purpose and from the start, and not just accepted after it already happened.

keyTerms.meaning: Taught publicly, as a public lesson
We examine (an expert checks whether the blemish is permanent)
From the start, permitted even before the act

phrases.english: Rabbah bar Rav Huna taught publicly:
If it was born with its blemish,
we examine it on the Festival from the start.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a practical ruling on the last clause of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בכור born with its blemish may be examined on יום טוב לכתחילה.

steps.title: רב נחמן objects: his father taught that the examination is only valid after the fact
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן quotes his father, who taught that the examination works only בדיעבד, and challenges רבה בר רב הונא's ruling that it is allowed לכתחילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to him: My father taught that if someone went ahead and examined it, it counts as examined. And you say we may examine it from the start?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן challenges רבה בר רב הונא using a teaching from his own father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'if he went ahead and examined it' describe something already done (דיעבד). That wording suggests the examination should not be done from the start. So רב נחמן says רבה בר רב הונא went too far by permitting it לכתחילה.

keyTerms.meaning: My father taught (quoting a ברייתא)
He went ahead and did it (even though he should not have)
It counts as examined

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן, אַבָּא תָּנֵי:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to him: Father taught:
If he went ahead and examined it, it is examined,
and you say we examine it from the start?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן, אַבָּא תָּנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling given in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה בר רב הונא's ruling that the examination is allowed לכתחילה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wording 'if he went ahead' only allows the act בדיעבד, so it is not allowed לכתחילה.

steps.title: אביי supports רבה בר רב הונא: the ברייתא has three parts, and the first allows only after the fact
steps.stepSummary: אביי says logic favors רבה בר רב הונא, because the ברייתא has three separate parts. The first part forbids examining לכתחילה a blemish that appeared before יום טוב, but allows it בדיעבד.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It makes sense to follow רבה בר רב הונא, because the ברייתא teaches three separate parts. First: if the blemish appeared before the Festival, we do not examine it on the Festival. This means it is forbidden from the start, but after the fact it is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי begins a proof for רבה בר רב הונא. He explains the first of the ברייתא's three parts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי reads each part of the ברייתא as a different level of permission. The first part, about a blemish from before יום טוב, says only 'we do not examine,' so it forbids לכתחילה but allows דיעבד. This sets up a contrast with the other two parts.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense, it is logical
Three parts (three clauses of the ברייתא)
After the fact, once it was already done
It is fine, it is acceptable

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: כְּוָתֵיהּ דְּרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא מִסְתַּבְּרָא,
phrases.english: Abaye said: It makes sense like Rabbah bar Rav Huna,
since it teaches three parts:

phrases.aramaic: נוֹלַד בּוֹ מוּם מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב —
phrases.english: If a blemish appeared on it on the eve of the Festival,
we do not examine it on the Festival.
It is from the start that it is not allowed,
but after the fact, it is fine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: כְּוָתֵיהּ דְּרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא מִסְתַּבְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends step 2 against רב נחמן's challenge in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: רבה בר רב הונא's ruling that examining is allowed לכתחילה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The three-part structure of the ברייתא, starting with its first part

steps.title: The second and third parts: forbidden even after the fact, and permitted even from the start
steps.stepSummary: The second part (blemish on יום טוב, per רבי שמעון) forbids the examination even בדיעבד. The third part (born with the blemish) must therefore allow it even לכתחילה, as רבה בר רב הונא ruled.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the blemish appeared on the Festival, רבי שמעון says it is not 'prepared,' meaning it is forbidden even after the fact. Then the ברייתא teaches again: everyone agrees that if it was born with its blemish, it is 'prepared,' meaning it is allowed even from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his proof by explaining the second and third parts of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part already allowed the examination בדיעבד, and the second part forbade it completely. So the third part would add nothing new unless it allows the examination לכתחילה. That is exactly what רבה בר רב הונא ruled.

keyTerms.meaning: And then it teaches again (a new, separate clause)
Also, even

steps.whatToRemember: In אביי's reading, each of the three parts teaches a different level: before יום טוב means allowed only after the fact, on יום טוב means not allowed even after the fact, and born with it means allowed even from the start. Steps 6-10 knock down this reading.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common גמרא method: if a teaching lists separate cases, each one must teach something new. Here, though, the proof depends on that ברייתא being reliable, and step 8 rejects it.

phrases.english: If a blemish appeared on it on the Festival,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אֵין זֶה מִן הַמּוּכָן —
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: This is not among the prepared,
meaning that even after the fact it is also not allowed.
And then it teaches:
And they agree that if it was born with its blemish,
that this is among the prepared,
meaning that even from the start it is also allowed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲדַר תָּנֵי: וְשָׁוִין שֶׁאִם נוֹלַד וּמוּמוֹ עִמּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the three-part proof begun in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: רבה בר רב הונא's ruling that examining is allowed לכתחילה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The second and third parts of the ברייתא, compared against the first
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to אביי's reading, a בכור born with its blemish may be examined on יום טוב even לכתחילה. This reading is rejected in steps 6-8, and step 10 concludes that it is allowed only בדיעבד.

steps.title: Rav Oshaya's ברייתא breaks אביי's three-level proof
steps.stepSummary: רב אושעיא brought a ברייתא in which the חכמים say that a blemish from before יום טוב and a blemish on יום טוב are both not מוכן. This undermines אביי's three-part reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: But when רב אושעיא came, he brought a ברייתא with him: whether the blemish appeared before יום טוב or on יום טוב, the חכמים say it is not מוכן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on אביי's proof by quoting a different ברייתא that tells the law in another way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's proof needed the first case, a blemish from before יום טוב, to be allowed בדיעבד. Only then would the born-with-blemish case have to be allowed even לכתחילה. In רב אושעיא's ברייתא, a blemish from before יום טוב is not מוכן at all, so the ladder falls apart and the born-with-blemish case could be allowed only בדיעבד, as רב נחמן said.

keyTerms.meaning: Here it means a ברייתא, a teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה
The day before the festival
Counted as 'prepared' before יום טוב, and so usable on יום טוב
'But isn't it so…?' This opens a challenge

phrases.english: But isn't it so that when Rav Oshaya came,
he came and brought a baraita in his hand:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין שֶׁנּוֹלַד בּוֹ מוּם מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: whether a blemish developed on it from the eve of the Festival,

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵין שֶׁנּוֹלַד בּוֹ מוּם בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: or a blemish developed on it on the Festival,

phrases.aramaic: חֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֵין זֶה מִן הַמּוּכָן.
phrases.english: the Sages say: this is not among the prepared.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the premise of אביי's proof in steps 4-5.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that the first part of the ברייתא allows a blemish from before יום טוב בדיעבד, which would force the third part to mean לכתחילה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא says a blemish from before יום טוב is not מוכן at all. That removes the middle level of the ladder, so the born-with-blemish case can be allowed only בדיעבד.

steps.title: Then the earlier ברייתא is a problem
steps.stepSummary: If רב אושעיא's ברייתא is right, the ברייתא that אביי used, which presents the law differently, now seems hard to explain.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then that other ברייתא is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notes that the two ברייתות now contradict each other. This sets up the next step, which will explain the contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two ברייתות give different rulings for a blemish that appeared before יום טוב. Both cannot be right as they stand, so the גמרא asks what to do with the first one.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But then…', 'if so…'
It is difficult; there is a problem
That one, here the earlier ברייתא

phrases.english: But then that one is difficult!
phrases.notes: 'That one' is the three-part ברייתא אביי built his proof on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out the contradiction between the ברייתא in step 6 and the ברייתא in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The three-part ברייתא used by אביי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two ברייתות disagree about a blemish from before יום טוב, so one of them needs explaining.

steps.title: That ברייתא came from אדא בר אוכמי, who mixed things up
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא אביי relied on was taught by אדא בר אוכמי, who used to garble the teachings, so it cannot be relied on.
steps.simpleTranslation: That ברייתא is from אדא בר אוכמי, who would mix up the teaching and teach it wrongly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by saying the earlier ברייתא is not a reliable version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the three-part ברייתא is set aside, רב אושעיא's version stands. אביי's proof for רבה בר רב הונא no longer works.

keyTerms.meaning: A teacher of ברייתות whose versions were known to be mixed up
He garbles the teaching and teaches it that way

phrases.english: That one is from Adda bar Ukhmei,
who confuses the teaching and teaches it that way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty raised in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects one source as an unreliable version
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות are equally reliable, so they truly contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The three-part ברייתא is אדא בר אוכמי's garbled version. רב אושעיא's ברייתא is the reliable one.
steps.whatToRemember: With the three-part ברייתא set aside, אביי's proof for allowing the examination לכתחילה falls away.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: the משנה's wording supports this too
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says the משנה is precise in this direction. He quotes רבי שמעון and asks what 'its blemish is not recognizable' means. 'Not recognizable at all' cannot be right, because that would be obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: The משנה is also precise this way. רבי שמעון says: any animal whose blemish is not recognizable before יום טוב is not מוכן. What does 'not recognizable' mean? If it means not recognizable at all, that is obvious. Why would it need to be said?
steps.whatsHappening: A new proof begins from the wording of the משנה. This step sets up the question and rules out the easy reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the animal had no visible blemish before יום טוב, of course it was not prepared. The משנה would not need to say that. So the phrase must mean something less obvious, which the next step will explain.

keyTerms.meaning: Is precise; its exact wording proves the point
Recognizable, visible
If you say… (opens a reading that will be rejected)
It is obvious

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
The mishna is also precise this way.
As it teaches, Rabbi Shimon says:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין מוּמוֹ נִיכָּר מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב —
phrases.english: any animal whose blemish is not recognizable from the eve of the Festival
is not among the prepared.
What does 'its blemish is not recognizable' mean?
If we say its blemish was not recognizable at all,
that is obvious. Does it need to be said?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further proof from the משנה for רב נחמן's view, after the challenge to אביי succeeded.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's view that a blemish may be examined on יום טוב only בדיעבד.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wording of רבי שמעון in the משנה: 'כֹּל שֶׁאֵין מוּמוֹ נִיכָּר מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב'.

steps.title: A blemish not shown to a חכם is not מוכן: proof established
steps.stepSummary: The phrase must mean the blemish was visible but was not shown to a חכם before יום טוב to decide whether it was permanent or temporary. The משנה still calls the animal not מוכן, so the proof stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means the blemish was not shown to a חכם before יום טוב to decide whether it is permanent or temporary. Even so, the משנה teaches that it is not מוכן. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct reading of the משנה and draws the conclusion: 'learn from this.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a blemish that existed before יום טוב is not מוכן if no חכם examined it. That is just like רב אושעיא's ברייתא, so there is no ladder of three levels. The permission for a בכור born with its blemish is therefore only בדיעבד, as רב נחמן said.

keyTerms.meaning: A permanent blemish, which permits slaughtering a בכור
A temporary blemish, which does not permit it
It was shown to a חכם for a ruling
In any event, at least
Learn from this; the proof is accepted

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, דְּלָא אִתְחֲזִי לְחָכָם מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב
phrases.english: Rather, it was not shown to a Sage on the eve of the Festival

phrases.aramaic: אִם מוּם קָבוּעַ אִם מוּם עוֹבֵר.
phrases.english: to decide whether it is a permanent blemish or a temporary blemish.

phrases.aramaic: קָתָנֵי מִיהַת אֵין זֶה מִן הַמּוּכָן,
phrases.english: In any event, it teaches that it is not among the prepared,
learn from this.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָתָנֵי מִיהַת אֵין זֶה מִן הַמּוּכָן, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof started in step 9 by giving the only sensible reading of the משנה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A blemish not checked by a חכם before יום טוב is not מוכן even בדיעבד. So a בכור born with its blemish may be examined on יום טוב only בדיעבד, as רב נחמן said, and not לכתחילה.
steps.whatToRemember: Both רב אושעיא's ברייתא and the משנה's wording support רב נחמן: a blemish is examined on יום טוב only בדיעבד, not לכתחילה.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Not recognizable' does not mean the blemish was invisible. It means no חכם had ruled on it yet before יום טוב.

steps.title: Hillel asks whether מוקצה can apply to half of שבת
steps.stepSummary: הלל asks רבא whether an item can be מוקצה for only half of שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: הלל asked רבא: Is there מוקצה for half of שבת, or is there no מוקצה for half of שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. הלל asks רבא whether an item can be forbidden as מוקצה for just part of שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now we learned that what counts is whether the animal was ready before the day began. Now הלל asks about a middle-of-the-day change: if something becomes unusable during שבת, does it stay forbidden for the rest of the day?

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him (a real question that needs an answer)
Set aside; an item that may not be used or moved on שבת or יום טוב
For half of שבת, meaning for only part of the day

phrases.english: Hillel asked Rava:
Is there muktze for half of Shabbat
or is there no muktze for half of Shabbat?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about מוקצה, after the earlier discussion of a blemished בכור on יום טוב.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether an item that becomes unusable partway through שבת keeps its מוקצה status for the rest of the day.

steps.title: How could half-day מוקצה even happen?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the question is about, since status is set at בין השמשות for the whole day.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If it was fit at בין השמשות, it is fit all day. If it was not fit then, it is not fit all day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the question itself. It asks how there could be a case of מוקצה for only half the day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Status is set at בין השמשות, the moment שבת begins. If the item was usable then, it is usable all day. If it was not usable then, it is forbidden all day. So the question seems to have no real case.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How do we picture it?
Twilight, the moment שבת begins
It was fit, usable

phrases.english: What is the case?
If it was fit at twilight, it is fit.
If it was not fit, it is not fit?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether הלל's question has any real case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea of מוקצה for half of שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Status is fixed at בין השמשות for the whole day, so a half-day case seems impossible.

steps.title: The case: fit, then unfit, then fit again
steps.stepSummary: The question is about an item that was fit, became unfit during שבת, and then became fit again.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed for a case where it was fit, then was pushed away, then was fit again. What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the case behind הלל's question and asks it again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The item was usable at בין השמשות, so it was not מוקצה at the start. During the day it became unusable, and later it became usable again. The question is whether that middle stretch makes it forbidden for the rest of the day.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for (this case)
It was pushed away, became unfit
And then again

phrases.english: No, it is needed
where it was fit, and then became unfit, and then became fit again.
What is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12 by giving a real case where half-day מוקצה could happen.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Status is set only at בין השמשות, so there is no half-day case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is an item that was usable, then became unusable in the middle of the day, then became usable again.

steps.title: רבא: Yes, there is מוקצה
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that once the item became unfit, it stays מוקצה for the rest of the day.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There is מוקצה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers הלל's question. Once the item became unusable, it stays forbidden even after it becomes usable again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being pushed away in the middle of the day counts. Even though the item was fine at the start and becomes fine again later, the time it was unusable makes it מוקצה for the rest of שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: There is מוקצה; it stays forbidden

phrases.english: He said to him: There is muktze.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא answers the question as defined in step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An item that becomes unfit during שבת stays מוקצה for the rest of the day, even if it becomes fit again.

steps.title: Challenge from the בכור born with its blemish
steps.stepSummary: הלל challenges רבא from the ברייתא that calls a בכור born with a blemish מוכן, even though it seems to go permitted, forbidden, then permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him: They agree that if it was born with its blemish, it is counted as מוכן. But why? Say: this בכור was fit at first along with its mother. Once it was born, it became unfit. When he showed it to a חכם, it became permitted again!
steps.whatsHappening: הלל attacks רבא's answer with the ברייתא about a בכור born already blemished. That calf seems to be exactly the fit, unfit, fit-again case, yet it is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before birth, the calf could be eaten along with its mother if she were slaughtered. Once born it is a בכור and is forbidden until a חכם sees its blemish. After the חכם sees it, it is permitted again. If רבא were right, it should stay מוקצה, but the ברייתא says it is מוכן.

keyTerms.meaning: And they agree
And its blemish is with it, born already blemished
Along with its mother, as part of her
It became permitted

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the calf was forbidden before birth. Inside its mother it was permitted as part of her. It is the birth that suddenly makes it a forbidden בכור.

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ: וְשָׁוִין שֶׁאִם נוֹלַד וּמוּמוֹ עִמּוֹ
phrases.english: He challenged him: And they agree that if it was born with its blemish
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא from earlier on the דף, where רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון agree.

phrases.english: that this is among the prepared.
But why? Let us say:

phrases.aramaic: הַאי בְּכוֹר מֵעִיקָּרָא הֲוָה חֲזֵי אַגַּב אִמֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: This firstborn at first was fit along with its mother,
phrases.notes: Before birth, if the mother were slaughtered, the calf inside her could be eaten too.

phrases.english: once it was born, it became unfit,
he showed it to a Sage, and it became permitted!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ: וְשָׁוִין שֶׁאִם נוֹלַד וּמוּמוֹ עִמּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's ruling in step 14 using a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that there is מוקצה for half of שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The blemished בכור goes from permitted, to forbidden, to permitted, yet the ברייתא calls it מוכן. So being pushed away midway did not make it מוקצה.

steps.title: Judges were present at the birth
steps.stepSummary: אביי (or רב ספרא) answers that judges saw the blemish right at the birth, so the calf was never forbidden even for a moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said, and some say רב ספרא: For example, where judges were sitting there.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי, or according to some רב ספרא, defends רבא. The ברייתא is about a case where experts were standing there and judged the blemish the moment the calf was born.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the judges saw the blemish right away, the calf never had a moment of being forbidden. It went straight from permitted with its mother to permitted as a blemished בכור. There was no unfit middle stage, so the ברייתא does not contradict רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: For example; the case is where
Judges, experts who rule on blemishes

steps.whatToRemember: רבא holds there is מוקצה for half of שבת: an item that becomes unfit midway stays forbidden. The blemished בכור is not a problem because judges were present at the birth, so it was never forbidden even for a moment.

phrases.english: Abaye said, and some say Rav Safra:
For example, where judges were sitting there.
phrases.notes: They saw the blemish as the calf was born, so it was permitted right away.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב סָפְרָא: כְּגוֹן דְּיָתְבִי דַּיָּינֵי הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers הלל's challenge in step 15 and saves רבא's ruling.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The newborn בכור had a forbidden stage between birth and being shown to a חכם.
steps.terutzMaskana: Judges were present and saw the blemish right at birth, so there was never a forbidden stage, and רבא's rule still stands.

steps.title: Second version: רבא says there is no מוקצה for half of שבת
steps.stepSummary: Some say רבא told הלל the opposite: an item that becomes unfit and then fit again is not stuck as מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say רבא answered: there is no מוקצה for half of שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of רבא's answer. Here רבא rules that once the item is fit again, it may be used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version (Step 14), an item that became unfit stayed מוקצה for the rest of the day. In this version רבא says the opposite: being unfit for part of שבת does not lock it as מוקצה once it is fit again.

keyTerms.meaning: מוקצה for half of שבת: becoming forbidden partway through the day

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new opinion arguing with רבא. It is a second report of what רבא himself said, and it is the opposite of Step 14.

phrases.english: Some say that he said to him:
There is no מוקצה for half of שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, opposite version of רבא's ruling in Step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An item that was fit, became unfit, and became fit again during שבת is permitted. It does not stay מוקצה.

steps.title: Support for רבא from the blemished בכור
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the ברייתא about a בכור born with its blemish supports this version of רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say the ברייתא supports him: they agree that a calf born with its blemish counts as prepared. But that בכור was fit at first along with its mother, became unfit when it was born, and became permitted when shown to a sage!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back the same ברייתא הלל used, but now as support for the new version of רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בכור goes permitted, then forbidden, then permitted again, yet the ברייתא calls it מוכן. That fits the rule that there is no מוקצה for half of שבת. The same source that was a challenge in Step 15 is now offered as a proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say it supports him: opens a suggested proof
By way of its mother: the unborn calf counts as part of the mother
Was pushed away: became unfit
Became permitted

phrases.english: Let us say that this supports him:
And they agree that if it was born with its blemish already on it,
phrases.notes: "They" are the תנאים who argue in that ברייתא. This is the same ברייתא from Step 15.

phrases.english: this counts as something prepared.
But this firstborn, at the start,
was fit to eat as part of its mother,
once it was born, it became unfit,
and when he showed it to a sage, it became permitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to back up the new version of רבא in Step 17.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's second version: there is no מוקצה for half of שבת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא that a בכור born with its blemish is מוכן, even though it went permitted, forbidden, then permitted.

steps.title: Rejecting the proof: judges were there at the birth
steps.stepSummary: אביי (or רב ספרא) answers that the judges saw the blemish right at the birth, so the בכור was never forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said, and some say it was רב ספרא: the case is where judges were sitting right there.
steps.whatsHappening: The proof is pushed away using the same answer as Step 16.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If judges approved the blemish at the moment of birth, there was never even a moment when the calf was forbidden. So the ברייתא is not a case of fit, unfit, fit again, and it proves nothing about מוקצה for half of שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Judges: experts who can permit a blemished בכור

phrases.english: אביי said, and some say it was רב ספרא:
For example, where judges were sitting right there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in Step 18 by limiting the case of the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected. רבא's second version is not disproven.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the calf was forbidden for a while. With judges present, it never was.

steps.title: New proof: grapes and figs left on the roof to dry
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: fruit put on the roof to dry may not be eaten on שבת unless it was designated before שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if someone was eating grapes, had some left over, and took them to the roof to make raisins, or figs to make dried figs, he may not eat them unless he designated them while it was still day. The same is true for peaches, quinces, and all other fruit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to test the question of מוקצה for half of שבת. This step sets up the next move, where the גמרא asks what case it means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fruit left to dry is set aside and not ready to eat, so it is מוקצה unless he designates it beforehand. The גמרא wants to see if this ברייתא shows an item going fit, unfit, fit again and staying forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Raisins
Dried figs
That he designates: sets the food aside for use
While it is still day: before שבת begins

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If he was eating grapes and left some over
and took them up to the roof
to make raisins out of them,
or figs, and left some over
and took them up to the roof
to make dried figs out of them,
he may not eat from them
unless he designates them while it is still day.
And you find the same
with peaches and quinces
and all other kinds of fruit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the בכור proof was rejected, the גמרא tries a new source.
steps.raayaObject: Whether there is מוקצה for half of שבת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about drying fruit that needs designation before שבת.

steps.title: What case is the drying-fruit ברייתא about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the fruit is dry, why designate it? If it is not dry, what good does designating do?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If the fruit is fit to eat, why does he need to designate it? If it is not fit, what good does designating it do?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to pin down the case of the ברייתא, because both simple options seem not to work. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the fruit is already dry, he put it up to eat later, so it should already count as ready. If it is still wet, designating it cannot make inedible fruit edible. So the ברייתא must be about some special case.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case?
Designation: setting food aside before שבת
What of it? It does nothing

phrases.english: What is the case?
If they are fit to eat, why does he need designation?
phrases.notes: "Fit" here means already dried enough to eat.

phrases.aramaic: אִי דְּלָא חֲזוּ — כִּי אַזְמֵין לְהוּ מַאי הָוֵי!
phrases.english: If they are not fit, when he designates them, what of it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the exact case of the ברייתא brought in Step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact situation of the drying fruit, since both 'fit' and 'not fit' seem to make the designation rule meaningless.

steps.title: Ruling out the case where the owner did not know whether the fruit was dry
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא considers saying that the owner did not know whether the fruit was dry. It rejects this because רב כהנא said that fruit set aside that dried is permitted even if the owners did not know.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say the case is where he did not know whether the fruit was fit or not, that cannot be. Didn't רב כהנא say that something set aside that dried is permitted, even if the owners are not aware of it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests one possible answer to its question from step 21 and knocks it down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea was that designating helps when the owner is unsure whether the fruit has dried. But רב כהנא rules that dried fruit is permitted even if the owner never knew it dried. So in that case designating would be pointless, and the ברייתא cannot be talking about it.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say (a suggested answer about to be tested)
That dried
The owners are not aware of it

phrases.english: And if you say, that he did not know
whether they were fit or were not fit,
phrases.notes: So his designating would mean: if they turn out dry, I want them.

phrases.english: but didn't רב כהנא say:
something set aside that dried,
and the owners are not aware of it,
is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא, דְּלָא יָדַע אִי חֲזוּ אִי לָא חֲזוּ, וְהָאָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects one possible answer to the question in step 21
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading the ברייתא as a case where the owner is unsure whether the fruit has dried
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: According to רב כהנא, dried fruit is permitted even without the owner's knowledge, so designating would add nothing

steps.title: The fruit was fit, became unfit, then became fit again, which proves מוקצה applies
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the ברייתא is about fruit that was fit, became unfit, and became fit again. Since the ברייתא requires designation, this seems to prove there is מוקצה in such a case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't the case where the fruit was fit, was pushed off, and then became fit again? And if you say there is no מוקצה in such a case, why would they need designation?
steps.whatsHappening: Having ruled out the other option, the גמרא proposes the case that would prove its point and spells out the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picture fruit that was edible before שבת, then was put out to dry so it became unfit, and then dried and became fit again. If such fruit were not stuck as מוקצה, no designation would be needed. Since the ברייתא requires designation, this seems to show that מוקצה does apply.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't it (introducing the suggested case)
They were pushed off (became unfit)
And then became fit again
Designating something ahead of time for use

phrases.english: Rather, is it not where they were fit and were pushed off,
and then became fit again?
And if you say there is no מוקצה,
why do they need designation?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו, דִּחֲזוֹ וְאִדְּחוֹ, וַהֲדַר אִחֲזוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting one reading, proposes the reading that yields the proof
steps.raayaObject: That an item which was fit, became unfit, and became fit again remains מוקצה (יש מוקצה)
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about fruit drying on the roof, which requires designation

steps.title: If there is מוקצה, how would designating help?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns the question around. If the fruit is truly מוקצה, then designating it before שבת should not help either.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what are you saying, that there is מוקצה? Then if he designates them, what difference does that make!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the proof from step 23 by showing that it creates a problem of its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If fruit that became unfit and then fit again is stuck as מוקצה, a designation would not cure it, since the fruit was unfit at the time. So reading the ברייתא as יש מוקצה does not explain why designation helps. The proof fails both ways, which means the case must be something else.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, what (are you saying)?
There is a מוקצה prohibition
What difference does it make?

phrases.english: Rather, what? There is מוקצה?
Then if he designates them, what of it!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מַאי יֵשׁ מוּקְצֶה? כִּי אַזְמֵין לְהוּ מַאי הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof just offered
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof in step 23 that the ברייתא shows יש מוקצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the item is truly מוקצה, designation cannot remove that status, so the יש מוקצה reading cannot explain the ברייתא either

steps.title: The case is half-dry fruit that some people eat and some do not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the ברייתא is about fruit that is partly dry. Some people eat it like that and some do not. Designating shows that the owner is one of the people who eat it, so the ברייתא proves nothing about מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed where the fruit was fit and not fit. There are people who eat it like this, and there are people who don't. If he designated it, he showed what he intends. If he did not designate it, he did not show what he intends.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new picture of the ברייתא that explains why designation helps. This also removes the proof from step 23.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fruit was never clearly unfit. It is only half-dry, and some people eat it that way. Designating simply tells us that this owner treats it as food. So the ברייתא has nothing to do with something that became unfit and then fit again, and it cannot settle the question.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for (a specific case)
Fit and not fit (partly ready)
People
He revealed his intention

steps.whatToRemember: The fruit-on-the-roof ברייתא does not prove anything about מוקצה. It deals with half-dry fruit, where designating shows that the owner considers it food.

phrases.english: No, it is needed where they were fit and not fit.
That there are people who eat them,
and there are people who do not eat them.
If he designated, he revealed his intention;
if he did not designate, he did not reveal his intention.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the difficulty in step 24 by redefining the case, which also defeats the proof in step 23
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא deals with fruit that was fit, became unfit, and became fit again, so it proves יש מוקצה
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא deals with half-dry fruit, where designating only shows the owner's intention, so it gives no proof about מוקצה

steps.title: רבי זירא begins a proof from beans and lentils
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא offers a new proof from beans and lentils. They start out fit to chew raw, and once they are thrown into the pot they become unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: Come and hear a proof from beans and lentils. Beans and lentils are fit to chew at the start. Once he throws them into the pot, they are pushed off.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא opens a new attempt to settle the question. This step sets up the case, and the proof itself continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Raw beans and lentils are fit at the start, so they are not מוקצה. When they are put in the pot, they become unfit for a while, since they are neither raw nor fully cooked. This is the first two stages of fit, then unfit, then fit again, the exact pattern the סוגיא is asking about.

keyTerms.meaning: Beans and lentils
To chew (eat raw)
Pot

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: תָּא שְׁמַע מִפּוֹלִין וַעֲדָשִׁים.
phrases.english: רבי זירא said: Come and hear from beans and lentils.
For beans and lentils
at the start are fit to chew,
once he throws them into the pot,
they are pushed off,
phrases.notes: While cooking, they are too soft to chew raw but not yet cooked enough to eat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: תָּא שְׁמַע מִפּוֹלִין וַעֲדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the fruit proof failed, opens a new proof attempt
steps.raayaObject: Whether an item that was fit, became unfit, and became fit again is מוקצה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The law of beans and lentils cooked on יום טוב
